pr.title: Add mailbox forwarding and automatic replies to the native API and panel
pr.body:
Adds administrator controls for mailbox forwarding and automatic replies through dedicated native commands, REST GET/PATCH /api/v1/domains/{domainId}/accounts/{id}/behavior and the responsive panel. Administrators can choose a forwarding destination, retain originals, configure spam-abort flags, set plain-text replies and manage expiration.

Native authorization enforces owning-domain and protected server-administrator boundaries; mailbox-user self-service remains pending. Validation checks complete requests before setters, rejects malformed/self forwarding, invalid dates, header controls, wrong types and unknown fields, and preserves omitted settings. Existing persistence, cache invalidation, per-sender suppression and server-local expiry behavior remain authoritative. No COM, direct web SQL or schema changes are added.

The panel loads settings separately, confirms active forwarding/reply changes, preserves literal text and explains external forwarding, storage, expiry and suppression. README, ROADMAP, requirements, architecture, REST documentation, CI inventory, AGENTS and the current AI handoff describe the implementation, tested boundaries and remaining Phase 1b work. UID modernization remains planned separately.

Validation: native and .NET compilation passed. In the checkpointed disposable Hyper-V VM, 26 DNS + 142 HTTP/security + 2 HTTPS + 188 live native assertions passed (358 total), plus 2 separate pipe-identity checks and expanded browser workflows/mobile layout. SMTP/POP3 probes deliver only between disposable local mailboxes and cover retained copies, forward-only, disabling, suppression, expiry and re-enabling. The first 40-second forwarding wait timed out; a queue-aware 100-second wait passed with the existing one-minute delivery poll. Original VM state was restored and its original mail service verified running. All 82 local Markdown links resolved and whitespace checks passed. No product runtime execution occurred on the development host.

Limitations: no indirect forwarding-cycle analysis or mailbox-user self-service; reply history remains in-memory and follows existing BO disable/persistence behavior. Production hosting, certificate lifecycle, Defender and PHP retirement remain later work. CI passed on exact head `99e0948261efad10279fc34f257d9b6efeca3374`: Release x64, all four database regression/management jobs, CodeQL, gcc/clang and installer publication. Each backend passed all 358 management assertions and browser workflows. NUnit totals stayed at 1,315 per backend: Compact/MySQL/PostgreSQL passed 1,205, failed 0, warnings 0, inconclusive 34, skipped 76; Express passed 1,206 with 75 skipped and the same other counts. This PR awaits maintainer review; it is not merged, and no next task starts without confirmation.

Native commands share the existing owning-domain and protected-server-administrator checks. They reject wrong types, unknown fields, invalid UTF-8/control characters and more than 16,000 UTF-8 bytes per format before writes, then use existing persistence/cache invalidation. Signature contents stay out of basic mailbox views. No COM, web SQL, schema change, domain-signature management or mailbox-user self-service is added.

The panel edits HTML as inert textarea source, confirms active changes, checks field/request byte limits, submits changed fields, preserves existing CRLF source when toggling and writes plain-text edits with CRLF for the existing HTML fallback. It does not render or sanitize email markup. Existing domain override/append/local-mail/reply policy, macros, large-message limits and MIME behavior remain authoritative.

Validation: native and .NET builds passed. Disposable-VM tests passed 26 DNS + 152 HTTP/security + 2 HTTPS + 224 live native assertions (404 total), plus two separate pipe-identity assertions and browser workflows. Signature probes cover authorization, input/persistence/Unicode, no partial invalid writes, preserved behavior settings, plain/HTML/multipart SMTP-to-POP3 delivery, address macros and disable/cache invalidation, with only disposable local recipients. Browser coverage includes inert source, confirmations/cancellation, UTF-8/request limits, mobile layout and omission/line-ending preservation. The CRLF omission regression failed before the fix and passed afterward; final browser files were rerun successfully. Original VM state was restored, its original mail service verified running, and only original Ready checkpoints remain. No product runtime tests ran on the development host. All 83 local Markdown links and whitespace checks passed.

Every backend passed all 404 management assertions and expanded browser workflows.
